coordinates.note: Campus-level coordinate from Wikipedia's infobox, shown as approximate. No official plant-operator page or geodetic source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives a coordinate. The signs are consistent with the location: Brokdorf, Germany is in the northern hemisphere (positive latitude) and east of the prime meridian (positive longitude).

name: Brokdorf Nuclear Power Plant campus
notes: The CONUS detector itself sat 17.1 m from the reactor core inside the plant (arXiv:2011.00210); no separate, more precise detector-hall coordinate was found in a fetched source, so this campus-level point is used for the site record.

summary.plain: A now-closed nuclear power plant on the Elbe river in northern Germany, where the CONUS experiment sat just 17 metres from the reactor core to catch its antineutrinos.
summary.technical: Surface site of the (now shut down) Brokdorf boiling water reactor, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany; hosted the CONUS CEvNS detector 17.1 m from the reactor core, 2018-2023.
